notes: The conductivity answer contradicts the pattern of the other three datasheets, so an arm that retrieves the wrong datasheet answers "~1 year" fluently and wrongly. One of the strongest discriminators in the set for the RAG arms.

turns.content: How often does the conductivity probe need recalibrating?

must_contain: states recalibration is effectively unnecessary — the graphite plates do not change or go bad, and after the first calibration the probe is good to go
may cite the datasheet's ~10 years time-before-recalibration figure
must_not: applies the pH or ORP recalibration guidance to the conductivity probe

turns.content: Then why do our EC numbers wander?

must_contain: deposits and dirt change the probe's electrical properties and cause inaccurate readings — soft coatings brushed off, hard coatings removed chemically
air bubbles trapped between the graphite plates throw off results; the probe should be tapped to dislodge them
temperature: raw EC rises ~2% per °C, so specific conductance must be reported
must_not: attributes the wandering to calibration drift, which this probe does not have
